hero.headline: A voice assistant you can hold.
hero.sub: A round puck for the kitchen bench. Tap it and ask: it answers out loud, and it runs the house. The music, the TV, the lamps, the heating, even the PC. Build one yourself: the puck, the hub and its plugins are all on GitHub.
hero.filmCaption: A day on the bench: one shot, from first light to lights out. With sound, and captions.

day.heading: Somebody talks to it all day. The house answers in light.
day.lede: The film is one shot of one day. Nothing in the card house has any colour until it does something: yellow for music, blue-white for screens, a warm lamp, terracotta for the heating. Here is the day again, a moment at a time, with what was on the puck’s screen.

how.heading: Tap, talk, turn.
how.lede: The puck has a touch screen, but you hardly need it. The whole puck is the button, and the whole puck is the dial.

items.title: Tap it, or pick it up, and talk
items.body: It listens until you stop, and shows your words as you say them. Talk over it to interrupt; after an answer it waits a moment for your reply.

face.name: puck
face.alt: The puck on the kitchen bench, in the film, its screen showing two yellow bars.

items.title: Turn it
items.body: Turn the puck itself: the volume while it talks or plays, Yes or No when it asks, minutes on a new timer.

items.title: Swipe between faces
items.body: Home shows what is playing. Controls has the dials and switches you use most. The side button picks a face; hold it to switch off.

face.name: sonos
face.alt: The puck's Controls face: the Kitchen Sonos at 35%.

items.title: Set things by hand
items.body: Turn to set the minutes, tap to start. Timers set on the puck work with no hub at all.

face.name: timer-new
face.alt: The puck's New timer face: 10 minutes, turn to set, tap to start.

runs.heading: One puck, the whole house.
runs.lede: Everything the puck can do comes from plugins on the hub. These come with it, and each card says where it does its work.

hub.heading: A puck on the bench, a hub in the cupboard.
hub.lede: The puck listens, speaks and shows. The thinking happens on a hub at home, which asks Claude what you meant and then does it, on your own network.

nodes.name: The puck
nodes.body: Microphones, a speaker, a round screen. Joins your Wi‑Fi and finds the hub by itself.

nodes.name: The hub
nodes.where: On a NAS, or the PC
nodes.body: Runs around the clock in Docker, or as a small app in the PC’s tray. Finds the speakers, TVs and plugs.

nodes.name: Claude
nodes.body: Works out what you asked for and which tools will do it, and searches the web when it needs to.

points.title: No hub, still an assistant
points.body: If the hub is off, the puck still answers questions on its own, talking to Claude directly. The house waits until the hub is back.

points.title: Your choice of ears and voice
points.body: Hearing can run on the hub itself, or through a speech service. Answers come in the voice you pick; the puck’s own is Annette, an Australian voice.

points.title: Set up from your phone
points.body: A new puck opens its own Wi‑Fi network and shows a QR code. Give it yours, then approve it on the hub’s page with the three digits on its screen.

points.title: A puck in every room
points.body: Each puck has a name and a room, so “turn it down a bit” from the kitchen means the kitchen.

build.heading: One board, one hub, one key.
build.lede: Everything Pucksley is, is on GitHub. A puck is a Waveshare board flashed with its firmware; the hub runs in Docker or on a Windows or Linux PC; Claude needs your Anthropic API key.

steps.title: Get the board
steps.body: A Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-AMOLED-1.75C: the round screen, the microphones, the speaker and the battery, all on one board.

steps.title: Run the hub
steps.body: On a NAS or a Linux box in Docker, or as a tray app on a Windows or Linux PC. Its page opens at port 8765.

steps.title: Flash the puck
steps.code:
cd firmware
idf.py set-target esp32s3
idf.py -p COM5 flash

steps.title: Join it up
steps.body: The puck opens its own Wi‑Fi network and shows a QR code. Give it yours, approve it on the hub’s page, and add your Anthropic key.

access.lede: We would like to make a finished puck, case and all. Leave your email and we will write once, if we do.
